sources.title: New Towns Draft Programme
sources.verified_claim: The government's draft programme assessed Crews Hill and Chase Park as a potential new town of up to 21,000 homes, while explicitly recognising significant natural-landscape impacts requiring mitigation and comprehensive masterplanning.

sources.title: Report: New Towns for London
sources.verified_claim: The adopted report says London new towns could support housing demand but require strong leadership, clear planning, transport from day one, green infrastructure, affordable housing and dedicated funding to avoid poor outcomes.

sources.title: MD3515 London Plan – publication and statutory consultation
sources.verified_claim: The Mayor approved the Draft London Plan for formal statutory consultation beginning 16 July 2026 for 13 weeks; it is a draft policy layer, not adopted parcel evidence.

sources.title: London Social and Affordable Homes Programme 2026-36
sources.verified_claim: City Hall's 2026-36 programme provides up to £11.7 billion for social and affordable housing, with at least 60% of programme homes expected to be social rent and funding available for projects able to start by March 2036.

sources.title: London’s affordable housing delivery falls short
sources.verified_claim: The 2026 Affordable Housing Monitor reports 14,335 starts under the 2021-26 programme by March 2026, below the revised 17,800-19,000 target, providing a regional delivery-capacity caution rather than a parcel-level conclusion.

sources.title: Enfield New Town (1)
sources.verified_claim: The Mayor stated the proposed Enfield New Town remained at a very early stage with no final development boundary; grey-belt extent could not be stated.

sources.title: Enfield New Town (2)
sources.verified_claim: The Mayor confirmed submitted Local Plan allocations at Crews Hill and Chase Park are within Green Belt but said the proposed New Town development boundary had not been finalised.

sources.title: Havering’s Place in London
sources.verified_claim: The London Assembly agreed a motion supporting Havering remaining within Greater London and emphasised continued strategic cooperation across transport, housing, economic development and environmental policy.
